cards.front: What must a first-time applicant for a license, permit or ID card bring?
cards.back: A first-time applicant for a license, learner's permit or ID card must bring originals or verifiable certified copies proving identity, lawful status in the US and full Social Security number, plus two documents proving Indiana residency.

cards.front: What should someone renewing or replacing an Indiana credential bring to get a Real ID?
cards.back: Someone renewing, amending or replacing a current Indiana credential should bring original or certified documents to a branch if they want a Real ID-compliant credential.

cards.front: What kind of US birth certificate proves identity, and which kind is refused?
cards.back: A US birth certificate used as identity proof must be an original or certified copy issued by a government agency, and unofficial hospital birth certificates are not accepted.

cards.front: When can a US passport or passport card prove identity?
cards.back: A US passport or passport card can prove identity only if it is not expired.

cards.front: When does a foreign passport prove identity?
cards.back: A foreign passport proves identity only when it is unexpired and carries a US visa with an approved I-ninety-four form showing the most recent admission or current status.
cards.memory_hook: unexpired, with visa and arrival record

cards.front: When can a Permanent Resident Card or Employment Authorization Card prove identity?
cards.back: A Permanent Resident Card or Employment Authorization Card can prove identity only if it is unexpired and its lawful status has been verified.

cards.front: What can a delayed birth certificate prove for someone born outside the US?
cards.back: A person born outside the US may use a delayed birth certificate to prove identity, but not lawful status.

cards.front: Can a delayed birth certificate prove lawful status?
cards.back: A delayed birth certificate for someone born abroad works for identity, while lawful status must be shown another way.

cards.front: What must be true of an amended birth certificate showing a new name or birth date?
cards.back: An amended birth certificate showing a new legal name or date of birth must be certified and filed with the vital statistics office in the state of birth.

cards.front: What can a non-citizen use as identity proof after getting a Real ID credential?
cards.back: A non-citizen who received a Real ID-compliant credential using one of the listed documents may use that credential as identity proof in later transactions.

cards.front: What must you show if your legal name or date of birth differs from your identity documents?
cards.back: If your legal name or date of birth differs from your identity documents, you must show legal proof of the change, such as a marriage license, divorce decree or court order.

cards.front: For a US citizen, what proves lawful status?
cards.back: For a US citizen, the document used to prove identity also proves lawful status.

cards.front: When does a Notice of Action count as lawful status proof?
cards.back: A Notice of Action on Form I-seven hundred ninety-seven counts as lawful status proof when the BMV confirms DHS has received it and not denied the action.

cards.front: Is proof of an asylum application a lawful status document?
cards.back: Proof of an asylum application verified by DHS is listed as a lawful status document.

cards.front: Which documents can prove your Social Security number?
cards.back: A Social Security number can be proven with a document showing your name and full number, such as a Social Security card, a W-two, a one thousand ninety-nine or a pre-printed pay stub.

cards.front: What does an applicant who does not qualify for a Social Security number submit?
cards.back: An applicant not authorized to work in the US who does not qualify for a Social Security number must submit documents showing that, and may be asked for a valid I-ninety-four instead.

cards.front: Who may list a post office box as a residential address?
cards.back: Only applicants in the Indiana Attorney General's Address Confidentiality Program may list a post office box as their residential address.

cards.front: Which bills and statements prove residency, and how recent must they be?
cards.back: A utility, credit card, doctor or hospital bill, a bank statement or a pre-printed pay stub can prove residency if it shows your name and residential address and is dated within sixty days of applying.

cards.front: How recent must an insurance policy be to prove residency?
cards.back: A homeowner's, renter's or vehicle insurance policy proves residency if it shows your name and residential address and is dated within one year of applying.

cards.front: How do the date windows for a W-two or tax bill and an insurance policy differ?
cards.back: A W-two, property or excise tax bill, or benefits statement must be dated in the current or prior year, whereas an insurance policy must be dated within one year of the application.
cards.memory_hook: this year, last year, or one

cards.front: Which voter and school documents are accepted residency proof?
cards.back: An Indiana voter registration card and public or private school records showing an enrolled student's name and residential address are among the accepted residency documents.

cards.front: Can a postal change of address confirmation prove residency?
cards.back: A US Postal Service change of address confirmation showing both prior and current address can prove residency.

cards.front: Who may file an Indiana Residency Affidavit?
cards.back: An applicant without two residency documents may file an Indiana Residency Affidavit if they are incapacitated, homeless, living with a relative or friend, or living in a motor vehicle.

cards.front: What must a relative or friend do to sign an affidavit for someone living with them?
cards.back: For an applicant living with a relative or friend, that person, aged at least eighteen, signs the affidavit at a branch and shows their own Indiana credential, identity proof and two Indiana address documents.

cards.front: Who signs the affidavit for an incapacitated applicant, and for a homeless applicant?
cards.back: For an incapacitated applicant the affidavit is signed by a resident guardian or caregiver aged at least eighteen, while for a homeless applicant it is signed by a representative of the agency or nonprofit that serves them.

cards.front: What does an applicant living in a motor vehicle need for the affidavit?
cards.back: An applicant living in a motor vehicle such as a motor home needs another Indiana resident to sign the affidavit at a branch and must show Indiana income tax payment plus current title and registration records with the BMV.

cards.front: Which documents does the BMV accept, and which may it refuse?
cards.back: The BMV accepts only original documents or certified copies from the issuing agency and may refuse any document that looks fraudulent, unreliable, altered or expired.

cards.front: What language must documents be in, and what must match Social Security records?
cards.back: All documents must be in English or come with a verifiably accurate English translation, and your legal name and date of birth must match Social Security Administration records.

cards.front: What must a document translation include?
cards.back: A translation must be typed on the letterhead of a government entity, accredited school or translation agency, with a signed statement of accuracy and competence, and not done for a family member, friend or business associate.

cards.front: What must a translator's statement say?
cards.back: A translator's statement must attest that the translation is accurate and that the translator is competent.

cards.front: What credential may a US citizen with a valid non-compliant card choose, and how is it marked?
cards.back: A US citizen holding a valid non-compliant Indiana credential may choose another non-compliant credential, which is printed with NOT FOR REAL ID PURPOSES on the front.

cards.front: What is the leading contributor to teen crashes?
cards.back: The leading contributor to teen crashes is errant, risky or distracted driving.

cards.front: How does each passenger affect a teen driver's crash chance?
cards.back: The manual says the chance of a crash doubles with each passenger in a teen driver's vehicle.

cards.front: Where do most multi-vehicle crashes involving teens happen?
cards.back: Most multi-vehicle crashes involving teens happen at intersections.

cards.front: Which factor is common in single-vehicle crashes, and which in multiple-vehicle crashes?
cards.back: Illegal or unsafe speed is a common factor in single-vehicle crashes, while driver inattention is a common factor in multiple-vehicle crashes.

cards.front: How do impaired teen drivers affect serious injuries and deaths in teen crashes?
cards.back: Teen drivers under the influence of alcohol or drugs are a small share but account for a much higher share of serious injuries and deaths in teen crashes.

cards.front: When should you not enter an intersection on a yellow light?
cards.back: Unless you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, you should not enter after it turns yellow.

cards.front: What should you be ready to do even on a green light?
cards.back: Even with a green light, be ready to stop as you approach an intersection in case the light changes.

cards.front: What does the manual say about phones and some over-the-counter drugs?
cards.back: Talking on the phone or texting while driving is against the law, and even some over-the-counter drugs can cause drowsiness.

cards.front: What habits are teens advised to follow with seats, mirrors, radio and music?
cards.back: Teens are advised to adjust seats and mirrors before each drive, wait until stopped to adjust the radio, and avoid loud music that could hide a siren or horn.

cards.front: What does the manual say about seat belts for teens?
cards.back: A seat belt is required by law and is the most effective way to lower the risk of being hurt or killed in a crash.

cards.front: When and in what conditions should parents practice driving with their teen?
cards.back: Parents are advised to practice driving with their teen during the learner's permit period and the first year of licensed driving, in varied conditions such as wet roads, snow, highways and night driving.

cards.front: What are parents urged to do for their teen driver?
cards.back: Parents are urged to set a good example, require seat belts, choose vehicles for safety rather than image, and grant progressive privileges as the teen shows good judgment.

cards.front: How does the manual describe driver education and the parents' role?
cards.back: The manual calls driver education a first step and says parents play a crucial role in teaching teens to drive.

cards.front: What must anyone under eighteen wear on an off-road vehicle?
cards.back: Anyone under eighteen operating or riding an off-road vehicle must wear a helmet meeting US Department of Transportation standards, and an owner may not knowingly let someone under eighteen ride without one.

cards.front: Where can an eligible person apply to register to vote during a credential transaction?
cards.back: Anyone eligible to vote may apply to register while completing a credential transaction at a branch, on myBMV.com or at a BMV Connect kiosk.

cards.front: What does the BMV do for a male under twenty-six who authorizes Selective Service registration?
cards.back: When authorized by a male under twenty-six getting a new or renewed license, the BMV sends his information to register him with the Selective Service, and failing to register is a felony.

cards.front: What penalties can failing to register with the Selective Service bring?
cards.back: Failing to register with the Selective Service can bring up to five years in prison and a 250,000 dollars fine, and registration applies to US citizens.

cards.front: Where are BMV forms available, and what about people not at a branch who want to register to vote?
cards.back: BMV forms are available on IN.gov slash BMV or at any branch, and mail-in voter registration forms exist for people not at a branch.

cards.front: How can vehicle registration be renewed, and how long do plates and stickers take?
cards.back: Vehicle registration can be renewed by phone, by mail, online at myBMV.com or at a BMV Connect kiosk, and for online, phone and mail renewals the plates and stickers arrive in about twenty-one days.

cards.front: How should checks for registration renewal be made out?
cards.back: Checks for registration renewal should be made out to BMV or Bureau of Motor Vehicles.

recap_hooks.text: First-time applicants prove identity, lawful status, Social Security number and residency with originals or certified copies.
Birth certificates must be certified, passports unexpired, and a delayed birth certificate proves identity only.
Bills and statements prove residency if dated within sixty days, and insurance policies within one year.
Without two residency documents, some applicants may file a Residency Affidavit.
The BMV takes only originals or certified copies, in English or with an accurate translation.
Errant, risky or distracted driving leads teen crashes, and each passenger doubles the risk.
Do not enter on yellow unless already in the intersection.
Riders under eighteen on off-road vehicles must wear an approved helmet.
You may register to vote during a credential transaction, and eligible males can be registered with Selective Service.
